author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: Rates, not earnings, are setting prices into the Fed decision: the 10Y at 4.88% with an inverted curve that steepened 24 bps over 20 observations from the long end means beats without raised guidance are punished, while the dollar is not amplifying the shock. Outside the US, China's PMI relapse and liquidity squeeze and Europe's Q3 contraction keep those regions Bearish, Australia faces a priced RBA hike, and Poland is the outlier, where a bank-led post-election re-rating is Bullish but must be hedged against a fiscal hole.
sources_policy: Every fact comes from a 2023-11-01 own-date headline cited in the same paragraph or from the 2023-11-01 market card; prices use each instrument's completed session (all 2023-10-31; Warsaw closed for the holiday on the report date), Treasury prior close 2023-10-31, crypto prior completed daily close 2023-10-31. Previews (Fed Wednesday, payrolls, Apple, Toyota, RBA, Orlen results, WeWork) are used only as pending events. No numeric spot-FX; currency direction only from cited reporting. No later-date files read.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n1506 (Reuters, yen sinks as BOJ adjustment seen inadequate) is stamped 2023-10-30 07:00 but describes the BOJ decision of 2023-10-31; both are before cutoff, so it is used only for the post-decision yen move.
n1020 (CBS, SBF trial reaches closing arguments) is date-stamped 2023-10-31 but closing arguments began on the report date; not used.
n0866 (Wccftech, AMD shares whipsaw after Q3) may describe after-hours trading near or past midnight UTC; not used, AMD is cited only via n0864/n1240.
Polish October flash CPI level and the RPP's October cut size are not in any own-date headline title; described qualitatively only.
n1521 and n1753 carry numeric FX levels in their titles; the numbers are not used.
Treasury's 2023-10-30 borrowing estimate has no own-date headline; only the pending refunding (n0101) is referenced.
n2062 (blog headline on September core PCE) is a non-standard annualised figure; not used.
